newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian business federation slams mini-budget.
newsitem.headline: Italian business federation slams mini-budget.

text.p: Italy's Confindustria business federation criticised a corrective mini-budget approved by the cabinet on Thursday and called for its withdrawal.

The package, intended to raise 15.5 trillion lire ($9.2 billion) in 1997 and cut the deficit to three percent of gross domestic product to keep Italy on track for entry to the European single currency, has yet to be passed by parliament.

Confindustria said in a statement after an extraordinary meeting in Rome that it wanted the package withdrawn and was calling a meeting in the capital of all its members -- potentially 110,000 people -- on April 10.
It said that meeting had been called "to demonstrate the opposition of businesses to this economic policy and decide what action to take.
"It's a package to be withdrawn. Its not serious," said Pirelli president Marco Tronchetti as he left the meeting.
The meeting would also assess possible legal moves concerning the legitimacy of the government's action in demanding that firms pay taxes on huge severance payment funds two years ahead of time.
The statement stressed Confindustria's "strongest opposition to the corrective package passed today by the cabinet, which contains further oppressive measures for business."
It warned that the measures would contribute to higher unemployment and depress the construction industry.
Confindustria also said it was worried that the mini-budget would make it harder for Italy to join economic and monetary union (EMU) from its start in 1999.
The body said that most of the measures were accountancy changes and one-off actions that would rebound heavily on state finances in future years.
